quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and nerves make you drowsy. This can affect your ability to ride safely. Know how a medication affects your body before you ride.

questions.question: How can you increase your ability to be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Make sure you always ride using your headlight.
Ride closely to vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you always ride using your headlight.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on at intersections. Choose a lane position that gives oncoming traffic the best view of you. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can take action if danger appears. Do not count on eye contact to keep you safe.

questions.question: If carrying a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be similar to the stopping distance of a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases how much force is needed to stop it. This means stopping distance may increase. Start slowing down earlier when riding with a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they can break away in the event of a crash.
Should not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time, they get scratched and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay protected and comfortable.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it signals a right turn or right lane change. You can use this hand signal instead of or along with your turn signals.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that keeps you safe. It should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, give you an escape route, and keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Fatigue can be increased by:

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: Dress for bad weather like wind and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit yourself to about six hours of riding per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not mean that they will yield to you when they should.
Guarantees that they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not actually notice them.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield. Drivers often look directly at a motorcyclist but fail to actually notice them.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.explanation: You need more space behind the vehicle ahead when it takes longer to stop. Wet pavement, poor visibility, and heavy traffic all require a larger following distance.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help a rider stay visible?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make wobbling worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, lean forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can also make wobbling worse.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot reach the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A properly fitting motorcycle allows your feet to reach the ground while you are seated. You should also be able to easily reach and operate all the controls.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, place it:

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads low and balanced on both sides. Placing loads too high can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect its balance.

questions.question: Which colors are best for riders to be seen?
questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: The extra weight of a passenger makes your motorcycle sit lower. Ride a bit more slowly, especially on curves and bumps. The extra weight also means it takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop, so keep a larger space cushion.

questions.question: Where are motorcyclists most likely to have conflicts with other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcyclists and other drivers. Be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away. Then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and let the bike slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away. Then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake again smoothly.

questions.question: One rider in a group wants to go faster than the others. What should the group do?

options.text: Let that rider go ahead. Meet up later at a planned spot.
Speed up so everyone stays together.
Split up. Let each rider go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let that rider go ahead. Meet up later at a planned spot.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them go ahead. Plan to meet at a specific spot later.

questions.question: What clothing gives a motorcyclist the best protection?

options.text: Shoes that do not cover the ankles.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear boots or tall shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually found?
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: A motorcycle that fits you properly should:

options.text: Let you touch the ground with your feet while sitting down.
Have a seat level with your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above your waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let you touch the ground with your feet while sitting down.
questions.explanation: A properly fitted motorcycle lets you reach the ground with your feet while seated. Always keep your feet firmly on the footrests while riding.
